done_when: The commit hook refuses only when git commit itself is given -n or --no-verify, never for an -n that belongs to another command on the same line

findings.body: Raise: Security. At line 209, the scanner treats `#` after an escaped space as a comment. In `echo x\ #note; git commit -n`, the shell treats `#note` as part of the argument and executes the commit, but the scanner discards everything from `#` onward. The hook therefore allows a commit that skips hooks.
findings.title: Escaped space lets a comment hide a prohibited commit

findings.body: Raise: Security. Line 219 treats a `cat` heredoc as inert whenever there is no pipe on its opener line. For `cat > script.sh <<'EOF'` with `git commit -n` in the body, followed by `bash script.sh` in the same command, the hook removes the commit from inspection even though the shell executes it.
findings.title: A heredoc written to a script hides a prohibited commit

findings.body: Raise: Not done. Line 216 recognizes a stdin commit message only for literal `git commit -F -`. A valid `git -C web commit -F - <<'EOF'` message containing `git commit -n` is retained and parsed as a command, so the hook refuses a commit that has neither prohibited option. The same gap affects `git commit --file=-`. The named allowed proof covers only literal `git commit -F -`.
